## Learning physical systems for control and optimization

A learned model of a physical system is usually fitted to answer a numerical question and then used to answer an operational one. The state may be a temporal quantity such as urban water demand or network pressure, or a distributed field fixed by initial conditions, geometry, boundary conditions, and external forcing. In both cases I judge the learned representation by the schedule, the control action, or the design computed from it.

The same test carries across coupled water-energy operation and materials processing. Decision-focused forecasting connects temporal uncertainty to operating cost, while a neural operator maps process conditions to a spatiotemporal field. Control and constrained optimization then check whether that field still carries the rollouts and sensitivities a process decision needs.

## Decision-focused forecasting under uncertainty

Forecast error matters differently once a prediction fixes an operating schedule. In coupled water-energy systems, [Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSG.2025.3601238) trains a probabilistic electricity-cost forecast through the stochastic water-supply schedules it induces, and a differentiable upper bound on the optimality gap returns the change in scheduling cost to the predictor.

Two further studies ask where the prediction error comes from. [Lag-free demand forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2024.124508) treats the delayed reaction near a demand turning point as a timing error, and [uncertain pressure regression](https://doi.org/10.1109/TCSS.2023.3272330) separates the response to observed inputs from the residual variation left by disturbances no sensor reports. Both are measured on response timing and disturbance sensitivity rather than on average numerical error.

## Neural operators for distributed dynamics

Many control and design problems depend on a field that evolves in space and time. I study neural operators that map initial conditions, geometry, boundary conditions, and forcing fields to the solution field, and I evaluate them on field error, rollout error, and the sensitivities that control and optimization read.

## Learning-based control

A learned solution operator supplies state rollouts without solving the governing equations again at every control step, which raises the question of how far its error travels. I study how approximation error accumulates over a control horizon and how much of it reaches the selected action, the closed-loop cost, and the constraint violation. Those quantities give training and evaluation criteria a control engineer can act on.

## AI for materials processing

With Professor Fengqi You, I develop neural operators that map process conditions, geometry, boundary inputs, and external forcing to evolving material state fields. Their rollouts and local sensitivities are then used in process control and constrained optimization.

Feasibility, objective value, and decision sensitivity test whether approximation error changes the selected operating condition or the physical design. This repeats the test I apply to water-energy systems, where a learned representation is worth only as much as the decision it supports.

## Related collaborative work

Collaborative work on generated actions asks how a learned trajectory satisfies geometric and decision constraints. [DRIFT](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2026.133261) stores local LiDAR geometry as graph memory during recurrent diffusion and evaluates the generated motion on endpoint error, clearance, smoothness, and runtime.

## Research map

| Research direction | Main question | Evaluation |
|---|---|---|
| Decision-focused forecasting under uncertainty | Which prediction errors change an operating decision? | Optimality gap, operating cost, response timing, and disturbance sensitivity |
| Neural operators for distributed dynamics | What solution field follows from new physical conditions? | Field error, rollout error, and sensitivity error |
| Learning-based control | How does model error change a control action? | Closed-loop cost and state constraint violation |
| AI for materials processing | Does the learned solution map preserve the process decision? | Objective value, feasibility, and decision sensitivity |

[First- and last-author publications](/publications/) carry the evidence behind these directions.
